findings.title: Human review references are not authenticated ground truth
attack_path: A caller claims a human identity and supplies unsupported passing references.
The controller accepts structurally complete review assessments.
An operator could mistake accepted synthetic status for real-world validity.
evidence: Reviewer and real-task evidence are references, not cryptographic attestations.
Reports deny promotion and deployment authority.
findings.recommendation: Require independent real-task outcomes and approval before optimization.

findings.title: Synthetic objectives remain non-executable untrusted data
attack_path: A caller stores crafted objective or evaluation text.
The controller bounds, scans, hashes, and stores it as untrusted data.
No command executes, routes, trains, invokes a provider, or changes policy.
evidence: Synthetic rows never enter tasks, replay, memory, skills, or project state.
findings.recommendation: Keep future execution behind replay isolation and privacy boundaries.

findings.title: Closed schemas and parameterized SQL bound persisted data
attack_path: A caller submits malformed, oversized, duplicate, or secret-like JSON.
Closed parsers and constraints reject it before a complete write.
Parameterized inserts prevent content from changing SQL structure.
evidence: Requests cap classes, variants, cases, text, JSON, and evidence.
Focused tests cover invalid input, secrets, and immutable rows.
findings.recommendation: Preserve closed schemas and migration constraints.

findings.title: Containment blocks writes and accepted suites cannot promote
attack_path: A caller attempts writes during containment or treats a review as authorization.
Safe Mode blocks both mutation paths.
Reports keep promotion and deployment authority false.
evidence: Direct Safe Mode paths are tested.
No training, provider, shell, network, promotion, or deployment command exists.
findings.recommendation: Require separate real-task benchmarks and approval downstream.

limitations: Reviewer identity and evidence references are not cryptographically authenticated.
Structural diversity does not prove semantic difficulty, fairness, or absence of contamination.
No semantic leakage detector, model generator, executor, training, promotion, release, or deployment is provided.
